concepts.name: Economic Survey: Nature, Authorship, and Constitutional Status
key_dimensions: Prepared by Economic Division of DEA under Chief Economic Adviser (CEA) — NOT a constitutional document
Presented before Union Budget (typically one day prior) — convention, not legal mandate
Tabled in both Houses of Parliament but does NOT require parliamentary approval
Distinction from Budget: advisory vs. binding; survey vs. appropriation

concepts.name: GDP Growth Rate: Measurement Methodology and Base Year Revisions
key_dimensions: GDP at constant prices (real GDP) vs. GDP at current prices (nominal GDP) — Economic Survey uses both
Base year revision (2011-12 series by CSO/MoSPI) and its impact on growth numbers
GVA vs. GDP: GDP = GVA + Product taxes – Product subsidies — survey often highlights GVA for sectoral analysis
Advance Estimate vs. First Revised Estimate — survey timing and data reliability traps

concepts.name: Fiscal Deficit and FRBM Targets as Tracked in Economic Survey
key_dimensions: Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure – Revenue Receipts – Non-debt Capital Receipts (NOT total receipts)
FRBM Act targets: Fiscal deficit, Revenue deficit, Debt-to-GDP ratio — survey tracks deviations and escape clauses
Distinction: Fiscal deficit vs. Revenue deficit vs. Primary deficit (Primary = Fiscal deficit – Interest payments)
Effective Revenue Deficit (introduced by FRBM Amendment 2012) — grants for capital asset creation excluded

concepts.name: Current Account Deficit (CAD) and Balance of Payments Analysis
key_dimensions: CAD = Trade deficit + Net invisibles deficit — survey tracks CAD as % of GDP (sustainable threshold ~2.5%)
Invisibles account: Services, remittances, income — India's structural surplus in services offsets goods deficit
Capital Account vs. Current Account: financing CAD through FDI, FPI, ECB — vulnerability analysis in survey
BoP crisis indicators: Forex reserve adequacy (import cover months), Guidotti-Greenspan Rule reference

concepts.name: Inflation Indicators: CPI vs. WPI — Survey's Analytical Framework
key_dimensions: CPI (Consumer Price Index) is RBI's target variable (flexible inflation targeting: 4% ±2%) — NOT WPI
WPI covers only goods; CPI covers goods AND services — WPI has higher weight for manufactured products
Core inflation vs. Headline inflation distinction: food and fuel excluded in core — survey uses both for policy signals
GDP Deflator as third inflation measure used in survey — broader than CPI/WPI, no fixed basket

concepts.name: India's External Debt: Composition and Vulnerability Indicators
key_dimensions: External debt classified by maturity (short-term vs. long-term) and creditor type (government vs. commercial)
Key vulnerability ratios tracked in survey: External debt-to-GDP ratio, Debt service ratio, Short-term debt to forex reserves
ECB (External Commercial Borrowings) as dominant component — automatic vs. approval route distinction
NRI deposits (NRE, FCNR-B, NRO) counted in external debt — interest rate and exchange rate risk
UPSC trap: Short-term debt by residual maturity vs. original maturity — survey uses residual maturity

concepts.name: Investment Rate and Savings Rate: Survey's Structural Analysis
key_dimensions: Gross Capital Formation (GCF) = Fixed investment + Change in stocks + Valuables — NOT just infrastructure
Household savings vs. Private corporate savings vs. Government savings — declining household financial savings trend
Investment-Savings gap = CAD — fundamental macroeconomic identity tracked in survey
Public vs. Private investment crowding-in/crowding-out debate — survey's stance on capital expenditure multiplier

concepts.name: Agricultural Sector Indicators: MSP, Terms of Trade, and Structural Issues
key_dimensions: Terms of Trade for agriculture (ratio of prices received to prices paid by farmers) — survey tracks deterioration
MSP coverage: 23 crops recommended by CACP — but legal guarantee status is a policy debate, not current law
Agricultural GVA growth vs. farm income growth — distinction important as GVA excludes farm subsidies impact
Disguised unemployment and underemployment in agriculture — survey's structural transformation argument

concepts.name: Manufacturing and Industrial Sector: IIP and Its Limitations
key_dimensions: IIP (Index of Industrial Production) — base year 2011-12, released by MoSPI with 6-week lag
IIP components: Mining, Manufacturing, Electricity — Manufacturing has ~77.6% weight (trap: not 'industry')
Use-based classification: Primary goods, Capital goods, Intermediate goods, Infrastructure/Construction goods, Consumer durables, Consumer non-durables
IIP vs. GDP manufacturing: IIP is volume index; GDP manufacturing includes unorganised sector — divergence trap

concepts.name: Services Sector: Composition, GVA Contribution, and Trade in Services
key_dimensions: Services = ~55% of GDP — largest sector but second-largest employer (behind agriculture)
IT-BPM, financial services, real estate, trade, hotels, transport tracked separately in survey
India's services trade surplus: key offset to merchandise trade deficit — WTO GATS commitments linkage
Productivity paradox: High GVA share but lower employment share compared to manufacturing — survey's structural concern

concepts.name: Tax Revenue Trends: Direct vs. Indirect Tax Buoyancy
key_dimensions: Tax buoyancy = % change in tax revenue / % change in GDP — value >1 means tax grows faster than economy
GST as unified indirect tax: CGST, SGST, IGST, CESS — survey tracks GST buoyancy post-implementation
Direct tax-to-GDP ratio vs. OECD average — India's low ratio (~6%) reflects low formalization and tax base
Tax expenditure (revenue foregone through exemptions) — survey highlights this as hidden fiscal cost

concepts.name: Government Expenditure Quality: Capital vs. Revenue Expenditure Analysis
key_dimensions: Revenue expenditure vs. Capital expenditure — survey advocates higher capex for growth multiplier effect
Effective capital expenditure = Budgetary capex + Grants-in-Aid for capital asset creation to states
Revenue deficit implies government borrowing for consumption — structural concern highlighted in every survey
Committed expenditure (salaries, pensions, interest) as % of revenue receipts — fiscal space indicator

concepts.name: Financial Sector Health: NPA Ratios and Credit Growth Indicators
key_dimensions: Gross NPA ratio vs. Net NPA ratio: Net NPA = Gross NPA – Provisions — survey tracks both for banking health
Credit-to-GDP gap as early warning indicator of financial crisis (BIS methodology) — used in survey
Credit growth vs. Deposit growth divergence — implications for liquidity and monetary transmission
PSB vs. Private bank NPA differential — survey's argument for PSB recapitalization and governance reform

concepts.name: Human Development and Social Sector Indicators in Economic Survey
key_dimensions: HDI components: Life expectancy, Education (MYS + EYS), GNI per capita — survey links expenditure to outcomes
Public expenditure on health and education as % of GDP — India's low ratio vs. comparable economies
JAM Trinity (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile) — survey quantifies subsidy leakage reduction and DBT coverage
Survey's use of 'Quality of spending' concept: outcomes per rupee, not just expenditure levels

concepts.name: Trade Policy Indicators: Export Competitiveness and Import Dependency
key_dimensions: Merchandise exports vs. Services exports — India's comparative advantage in services (RCA index concept)
Import intensity of exports — survey tracks value addition in exports vs. re-export of imported inputs
Trade openness ratio = (Exports + Imports) / GDP — India's declining trade openness as a structural concern
Export basket diversification vs. concentration — HHI (Herfindahl-Hirschman Index) used in survey analysis

concepts.name: Employment and Labour Market Indicators: PLFS Data in Economic Survey
key_dimensions: PLFS (Periodic Labour Force Survey) by NSSO — four employment measures: UPSS, UPAS, CWS, CDS
Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) vs. Worker Population Ratio (WPR) vs. Unemployment Rate — definitional traps
Female LFPR in India: Among lowest globally — survey's analysis of social vs. economic determinants
Formal vs. Informal employment: EPFO/ESIC subscriber data used as proxy for formalization trend

concepts.name: Monetary Policy Transmission and Liquidity Indicators
key_dimensions: Repo rate as policy rate vs. Reverse repo, MSF, Bank Rate — survey analyzes transmission lag to lending rates
MCLR vs. External Benchmark-based lending rate (EBLR) — survey on incomplete transmission under MCLR regime
Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) corridor: width and implications for overnight rates
Real interest rate = Nominal rate – Inflation — survey tracks whether real rates are conducive to investment

concepts.name: State of the Economy Chapter: Survey's Composite Nowcasting Approach
key_dimensions: Survey uses high-frequency indicators (GST collections, PMI, E-way bills, power consumption) for real-time tracking
Composite Leading Indicators vs. Coincident Indicators vs. Lagging Indicators — survey's classification
Business Expectation Index and Consumer Confidence Index (RBI surveys) cited in Economic Survey
UPSC trap: Economic Survey's GDP forecast vs. RBI's vs. IMF's — different methodologies, different numbers

concepts.name: Debt Sustainability and Public Debt Management
key_dimensions: Debt sustainability condition: Nominal growth rate > Effective interest rate on debt (r < g condition)
Centre vs. States debt: General government debt = Central + State debt (net of inter-government loans)
Contingent liabilities (guarantees, off-budget borrowings) — survey highlights these as hidden fiscal risks
Debt monetization vs. Market borrowing — survey's analysis of RBI's role and inflationary implications

concepts.name: Economic Survey's Thematic Innovations: Concepts Introduced in Recent Surveys
key_dimensions: Thalinomics (2019-20): Cost of thali as welfare indicator — purchasing power of wages in real consumption terms
Bare Necessities Index (2020-21): Multi-dimensional measure of access to water, sanitation, housing, micro-environment, financial inclusion
V-shaped recovery framework (2020-21) vs. K-shaped recovery debate — survey's empirical defense of V-shape
Survey's use of 'Wealth of Nations' vs. GDP — natural capital accounting and beyond-GDP metrics
